name: password-reveal
title: Password Reveal Animation

overview.description: A modern and smooth password reveal animation that displays password characters one by one from left to right with an elegant ease-in timing curve. Features a clean UI with gradient background and interactive eye icon.
overview.purpose: Enhances user experience in login forms by providing a visually engaging way to toggle password visibility with character-by-character reveal animation.
overview.useCase: Login forms, authentication interfaces, password management systems

visualEffects: Eye icon transformation with slash line animation
Glassmorphism effect on input field (backdrop-filter blur)
Smooth transitions on hover and focus states
Subtle pulse effect during character reveal

keyFeatures: Cubic ease-in timing curve for natural acceleration

howItWorks.summary: The animation uses a JavaScript class that manages password visibility state. When the eye icon is clicked, the password is temporarily masked with bullet points (●), then each character is revealed sequentially with a calculated delay that creates an ease-in effect.
steps: Initial state: Password is shown as bullet points (●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●●)
User clicks eye icon: Animation begins after 150ms initial pause
Character reveal loop: Each character replaces a bullet from left to right
Timing calculation: Starts slow (120ms delay) and accelerates to fast (30ms) using cubic ease-in
Visual feedback: Subtle translateX pulse and opacity fade during reveal
Final state: Complete password is visible
Re-click: Password immediately returns to masked state
howItWorks.timingCurve: Cubic ease-in (1 - (1 - progress)³) - starts at 120ms delay, accelerates to 30ms
howItWorks.animationDuration: Variable based on password length (e.g., 20 chars ≈ 1.5 seconds)

integration.htmlStructure: Simple input wrapper with SVG icon button inside relative-positioned container
cssClasses: .eye-icon - SVG with eye path, pupil, and slash line
.active - button state when password is visible

methods: revealPassword() - async method for character-by-character reveal
maskPassword() - replaces text with bullet points

parameters.name: Reveal Speed
parameters.description: Adjust character reveal timing. Lower values = faster reveal.

parameters.name: Timing Curve
parameters.description: Change acceleration curve. Try quadratic (^2) for gentler, quartic (^4) for sharper.
parameters.example: const easeIn = 1 - Math.pow(1 - progress, 2); // Gentler acceleration

parameters.name: Initial Pause
parameters.example: await this.sleep(300); // Longer pause before reveal

optimizations: No external libraries - minimal bundle size (~9 KB total)
CSS transitions use GPU-accelerated properties (transform, opacity)
Event listener cleanup and prevention of rapid clicking
Efficient string concatenation for character reveal
No DOM manipulation during animation (value updates only)
considerations: Password is briefly visible in DOM during reveal (intentional UX feature)
Animation blocks during reveal to prevent state conflicts
Uses type='text' for reveal (security consideration for demo purposes)
Keyboard event prevention stops user editing during animation

features.backdropFilter: Safari requires -webkit- prefix (auto-handled by modern browsers)
features.cssVariables: All modern browsers support CSS custom properties

browserCompatibility.fallbacks: No explicit fallbacks - assumes modern browser environment

features: ARIA label on toggle button: aria-label='Show password'
Keyboard shortcut: Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + P to toggle
Focus indicators with box-shadow on input focus
Button has proper hover and active states
SVG icon is purely decorative (button has aria-label)
improvements: Could add role='button' to toggle button
Could announce password visibility state to screen readers
Could add aria-live region for character reveal count

codeExamples.basicUsage: // JavaScript const input = document.getElementById('password'); const button = document.querySelector('.toggle-password'); new PasswordReveal(input, button);

useCases: Modern authentication forms with enhanced UX
advantages: Responsive design works on all screen sizes
limitations: Password visible in DOM during reveal (design choice, not security flaw for demos)
Animation blocks user interaction during reveal
